code: set.seed(20260819) n_sites <- 3  # Same 6 cells as trial_design, but split into 3 site-level rows each, # with person_years randomly divided across sites (summing back to the # original cell total) and cases simulated per site. trial_design_by_site <- do.call(   rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(trial_design)), function(i) {   cell <- trial_design[i, ]   py_split <- as.numeric(     rmultinom(1, cell$person_years, prob = rep(1, n_sites)))   data.frame(     age_grp = cell$age_grp,     arm = cell$arm,     site = paste0("site", seq_len(n_sites)),     person_years = py_split,     cases = rpois(n_sites, py_split * cell$placebo_rate *       ifelse(cell$arm == "vaccine", true_rr, 1))   ) })) trial_design_by_site <-   trial_design_by_site[trial_design_by_site$person_years > 0, ] nrow(trial_design_by_site) #> [1] 18  # Aggregate back down to one row per (age_grp, arm) pattern: sum cases and # person_years within each group (no log() needed here, since this # vignette's offset_log = FALSE throughout; person_years is already the # raw exposure). trial_design_agg <- aggregate(   cbind(cases, person_years) ~ age_grp + arm,   data = trial_design_by_site,   FUN = sum )  fit_by_site <- ep_closed_form(   formula = cases ~ arm,   data = trial_design_by_site,   offset = "person_years",   offset_log = FALSE,   strata = "age_grp",   ref_levels = list(arm = "placebo"),   verbose = FALSE )  fit_agg <- ep_closed_form(   formula = cases ~ arm,   data = trial_design_agg,   offset = "person_years",   offset_log = FALSE,   strata = "age_grp",   ref_levels = list(arm = "placebo"),   verbose = FALSE )  # Identical estimate, CI, and p-value either way; aggregating first only # changed how many rows the dynamic program had to process, not the answer. all.equal(   fit_by_site$exactparmest[, c("Estimate", "LowerCL", "UpperCL", "PValue")],   fit_agg$exactparmest[, c("Estimate", "LowerCL", "UpperCL", "PValue")] ) #> [1] TRUE

title: Exact Conditional Inference for Poisson Regression
text: Exact conditional inference Poisson regression: exact conditional maximum likelihood estimates, exact p-values, exact confidence intervals categorical effects Poisson regression models optional offset stratification. Nuisance parameters (stratum intercepts model effects test) eliminated conditioning sufficient statistics rather relying asymptotic approximations. matters case counts small sparse standard Wald/likelihood-ratio inference unreliable (rare outcomes, small strata, vaccine/drug-safety signal detection, similar settings). Three algorithms provided different problem shapes: ep_closed_form(): fast closed-form method single two-level effect strata nuisance structure, following Guess, Lydick, Small Miller (1987) Guess Thomas (1990). ep_multi_shift(): multivariate shift algorithm arbitrary categorical covariates strata, generalizing Hirji, Mehta Patel (1987) bounded Poisson counts. ep_network(): network algorithm offering aggressive mid-computation pruning larger problems, generalizing Mehta, Patel Senchaudhuri (1992) bounded Poisson counts. recompute_exact_inference() lets caller ask different question (different null, significance level, CI type/direction) already-fitted result’s OUTDIST table without rebuilding . conditioning approach mirrors used SAS’s PROC GENMOD EXACT statement; users familiar procedure’s options output find terminology (EXACTMAX, OFFSET, OUTDIST) intentionally similar.

text: list : beta0: null value tested, echoed back. p_lower: lower tail probability beta0, \(\Pr_{\beta_0}(T \le t_{obs})\). p_upper: upper tail probability beta0, \(\Pr_{\beta_0}(T \ge t_{obs})\). pvalue_two_sided: twice smaller one-sided tail probability, capped 1 (package's two-sided exact p-value convention, matching SAS's PROC GENMOD EXACT statement). pvalue_one_sided: min(p_lower, p_upper). alpha: significance level used, echoed back.
